answer: Make influence proportional to an atlas of attested work rather than to the number of accounts. Each identity must complete useful jobs verified by unrelated peers, and its record grows slowly while idle identities decay toward the nadir of standing. Creating copies does not multiply power, because a newcomer must cross the same canyon of costly, time-bound proof as every other identity: separate hardware, separate funding, and a separate history that cannot be cloned. Identities that share proofs or funding are merged in the atlas and quarantined until peers vouch for them separately.
